name: the two internal registries: the cycles they broke, and the device lifetime they carry
environment: Needs nothing but Node -- no CNA library, no artifact, no browser. Every mutant below is either an architectural regression (a registry that starts importing the layer above it, or a resource module that reaches back into GraphicsDevice for state) or a device-lifetime defect in the extracted registry itself. The first kind is what made `cna-ts/extensions/devices` and `cna-ts/extensions/input` throw `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'Texture2D' before initialization` as a consumer's FIRST import while every gate in the package was green; the second is the half a cold import cannot see, because a registry that answers for a disposed device imports perfectly well. One mutant here -- `handle-lookup-stops-checking-disposal` -- SURVIVED its first run, because the test asserted the refusal with a loose `/GraphicsDevice/` and the released native lifetime raises an ObjectDisposedException carrying its own label, 'caller-created GraphicsDevice', which matched. The assertion now pins the exact message, which is the difference between measuring that the registry refused and measuring that something did. The deep-import rule this gate also carries is NOT planted here: a defect in a test page or a suite changes no built file, so the harness rebuilds `dist` byte-identical and rightly refuses a verdict. That rule is watched by a rejection case in `test/module-cycles.test.mjs` instead.

mutants.why: the graphics device registry takes a runtime import from the extension layer it sits below. Nothing throws and every test passes -- the module graph is simply back in the shape where an initialisation order decides whether a consumer's first import works. This is the regression the source-level half of the gate exists for, and it fails at the source rather than after a build

the registry imports GraphicsDevice as a value rather than as a type, which is the exact edge its extraction removed. The cycle closes again and takes 23 modules with it, the root barrel included -- so this one is caught twice over, by the rule and by the cold import

the original defect reduced to the one edge that caused it: Texture2D reaches GraphicsDevice.js at runtime again. `RenderTargets` then reaches `class RenderTarget2D extends Texture2D` with the base class still in its temporal dead zone. Five published entry points stop importing -- three more than the two that failed before the refactor, because the side-effect imports that used to paper over those two are gone with the cycle

disposal deletes the device's entry instead of marking it disposed. That looks like tidying up and is not: `GraphicsDevice.IsDisposed` is answered from the entry, so a disposed device begins reporting that it is not disposed, and every later lookup refuses with 'requires a CNA device route' -- the message for a device that was never constructed -- rather than by name

the mirror image: the entry survives disposal and is never marked, so the registry keeps answering for a device whose native handle has been released. Every accessor hands out a freed handle, and IsDisposed answers false forever

one accessor stops going through the disposal check and reads the map directly. This is the subtlest of the six, because a caller-created device's lifetime refuses on its own a moment later -- so the failure is not that nothing throws, it is that the WRONG thing throws, and a device whose lifetime is borrowed and still alive would not throw at all
